name: Carnegie Mellon
blurb: Buggy, buildings, presidents, alumni and the tech that started on a Pittsburgh hillside.
disclaimer: Made by a Carnegie Mellon faculty member for fun. Not an official university product, and no university logos or marks are used.

puzzles.title: My Heart Is in the Work
puzzles.intro: Andrew Carnegie's motto, and a grid full of Carnegie Mellon: a carnival weekend, the presidents on the buildings, inventions that started here, and four alumni whose names do double duty.
puzzles.explanation: PORTER looks like a building (Porter Hall), and WARNER sounds like show business, but Warner is a president with a hall of his own and Porter is Billy Porter of the drama school.

categories.label: SPRING CARNIVAL
categories.explanation: The buggy races through Schenley Park, the student-built booths on the Midway, and the Mobot race for small line-following robots.

categories.label: PRESIDENTS WITH A BUILDING
categories.explanation: Warner Hall, Cyert Hall, Doherty Hall and the Cohon University Center are named for four of the university's presidents.

categories.label: BORN AT CARNEGIE MELLON
categories.explanation: The "are you human?" test, an early search engine, the language app, and the Mach kernel that macOS still builds on.

categories.label: DRAMA ALUMNI WHOSE NAMES ARE WORDS
categories.explanation: Holly Hunter, Judith Light, Billy Porter and Josh Gad all studied in the School of Drama.

puzzles.title: Tartan Pride
puzzles.intro: Bagpipes on the lawn, names on the buildings, the people who started artificial intelligence here, and a few words you will only hear in Pittsburgh.
puzzles.explanation: NEWELL and SIMON share a building name (Newell-Simon Hall), so they tempt the buildings group, but they belong with the AI pioneers. And REDDY is a person, not "redd up."

categories.label: SCOTTISH SPIRIT
categories.explanation: The Scottish terrier mascot, the team name, the Kiltie Band, and the instrument you can earn a degree in here. Andrew Carnegie was born in Scotland.

categories.label: CAMPUS BUILDINGS
categories.explanation: Wean Hall, Hunt Library, the Gates Hillman Centers, and the Tepper Quad.

categories.label: AI PIONEERS ON THE FACULTY
categories.explanation: Allen Newell and Herbert Simon shared a Turing Award, Raj Reddy won one and was the Robotics Institute's founding director, and Scott Fahlman proposed the :-) emoticon in 1982.

categories.label: PITTSBURGHESE
categories.explanation: You all, nosy, slippery, and a rubber band.

puzzles.title: Carnival Weekend
puzzles.intro: Race day in Schenley Park. Find the buggy words, the alumni, the clubs in the bag, and four things that come after the word Carnegie.
puzzles.explanation: Every buggy has a DRIVER, but so does every golf bag, and the buggy group has enough words without it. GOSLING is James Gosling, who earned his PhD here and went on to create Java.

categories.label: GOLF CLUBS
categories.explanation: Four clubs in the bag. DRIVER is the trap: a buggy has one too.

categories.label: BUGGY LINGO
categories.explanation: Pushers run the uphill legs, the freeroll is the coast down Schenley Drive, the chute is the sharp turn at the bottom, and Sweepstakes is the race's official name.

categories.label: FAMOUS ALUMNI
categories.explanation: Andy Warhol (pop art), John Nash (game theory), James Gosling (the Java language), and Stephanie Kwolek (Kevlar), who studied at Margaret Morrison Carnegie College.

categories.label: CARNEGIE ___
categories.explanation: Carnegie Hall in New York, the Carnegie Deli near it, Carnegie Tech (this school's name until 1967), and the Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh, next door to campus.
